profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed to Prime, most likely Prime Data Centers given the California and Texas registry locations. Prime Data Centers own site states the company was established in 2017 in California and is now headquartered at 400 North Ervay Street, Dallas, Texas, under founder and CEO Nicholas Laag, and describes itself as majority founder owned. The company reports 28 data centers across 13 campuses globally with a 4 plus gigawatt expansion pipeline, and lists Silicon Valley and Dallas among its confirmed North America markets, alongside Austin, Chicago, Los Angeles, Phoenix, and Sacramento, matching both states where this registry lists a Prime facility. No building specific address, opening date, or individual MW figures for this particular registry row were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Prime Santa Clara publishes 57 MW of IT capacity across 540,000 square feet in Silicon Valley, making it the third-largest facility by published power in California and representing 16 percent of the state's 365 MW of published data center IT load. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 57 MW of IT load translates to roughly 1,425 racks, assuming full utilization for compute-intensive workloads. The campus holds SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS certifications, qualifying it for security-sensitive workloads and regulated computing.

California has mapped 103 data center facilities but publishes power figures for only 11. Prime Santa Clara ranks among the handful of sites in the state with disclosed capacity, placing it in a narrow set of campuses whose scale is known. The operator, Prime Data Centers, operates 28 facilities across 13 global campuses and reports a 4-plus gigawatt expansion pipeline, but individual facility opening dates and build-out timelines are not published.

The site's location in Santa Clara County, the heart of the technology industry, positions it for short hauls to major compute demand centers. Whether this campus is acquiring new load or serving existing tenants is not published. The grid serving Silicon Valley is not specified in the available data.
